title: The five pillars of Islam
preview: Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm, and Hajj form the foundation of a Muslim's faith and practice.
content:
# The five pillars of Islam

The five pillars are the core acts of worship that every Muslim is expected to fulfill:

## 1. Shahadah (Declaration of faith)

To believe and declare that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His messenger.

## 2. Salah (Prayer)

To perform the five daily prayers at their appointed times.

## 3. Zakat (Charity)

To give a portion of one's wealth to those in need, once a year if one meets the threshold.

## 4. Sawm (Fasting)

To fast during the month of Ramadan from dawn until sunset.

## 5. Hajj (Pilgrimage)

To perform the pilgrimage to Makkah at least once in a lifetime if one is able.

---

These pillars unite Muslims in belief and practice across the world.
reference: Based on hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: The six pillars of Iman
preview: Belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree.
content:
# The six pillars of Iman (faith)

A Muslim believes in:

**1. Allah** – One God, no partners, no equals.

**2. His Angels** – Created from light; they obey Allah and carry out His commands.

**3. His Books** – The Scriptures revealed to prophets, including the Quran as the final revelation.

**4. His Messengers** – From Adam to Muhammad (peace be upon them all).

**5. The Last Day** – Resurrection, judgment, Paradise and Hell.

**6. Divine decree** – That good and evil are by Allah's will and decree.

---

*Reference: Hadith of Jibril (Gabriel)*

title: Why Muslims pray five times a day
preview: The five daily prayers were ordained during the Prophet's Night Journey (Isra and Mi'raj).
content:
# The five daily prayers

Salah was made obligatory on the Night of Isra and Mi'raj, when the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was taken from Makkah to Al-Aqsa and then through the heavens.

Initially Allah commanded fifty prayers per day; after the Prophet's repeated requests, it was reduced to five. The five prayers are: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha.

---

*Reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 349, 7517*

title: The Quran is preserved
preview: Allah promised to preserve the Quran; it remains unchanged since revelation.
content:
# Preservation of the Quran

Allah says: *"Indeed, it is We who sent down the reminder (the Quran), and indeed We will be its guardian."* (Quran 15:9)

The Quran was revealed to the Prophet (SAW) over 23 years, memorized by the Companions, and written down in his lifetime. Today, millions memorize it entirely, and the text is identical worldwide.

---

No other scripture has been preserved in the same way – both in writing and in the hearts of believers.

title: Greeting in Islam
preview: As-salamu alaykum (peace be upon you) and the full reply.
content:
# The Islamic greeting

**As-salamu alaykum** – Peace be upon you.

**Reply:** *Wa alaykumu s-salam (wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuhu)* – And upon you be peace (and the mercy of Allah and His blessings).

The Prophet (SAW) said spreading salam increases love and strengthens bonds. The one who initiates the greeting is closer to Allah.

---

*Reference: Sunan Abi Dawud, Tirmidhi*
